_comment: Copy this to config.json and fill it in. Everything is optional: a device left
blank simply does not appear, and the room page carries on without it rather
than erroring. Fill it in as you pair each thing.
Addresses: use fixed IPs, reserved in your router by MAC. A device that moves
to a new address on its own is a wall panel that stops working on a Tuesday for
_allow_origins: Which pages may drive this. Echoed back rather than answering '*', because '*'
would let any page the iPad ever loads press buttons in your room. Add the
http://<mac-ip>:8000 origin too if you are testing with serve.py.

appletv._note: atvremote scan, then atvremote --id <id> --protocol companion pair

tv._note: Leave token empty. The TV shows an allow box on first contact and the token it returns is written back here automatically.

desktop._note: hdmi is optional: set it and waking the PC also switches the TV to it. Yours is not on the TV, so leave it out unless that changes.

sonos._note: Optional. SoCo discovers it on the LAN anyway; this only pins which one if you ever have two.

dyson._note: Serial and wifi credentials are on the sticker on the machine itself.

ceiling._note: id and key come from python3 -m tinytuya wizard. If commands time out, try version 3.4 or 3.5; the protocol version is per-firmware and guessing it is faster than finding out.

wled._note: No credentials. WLED answers plain HTTP on the LAN, which is why the strip is the one device here that owes nobody an account.
